answer_1.quote: We propose an algorithm to sample text nonautoregressively from a conditional or unconditional LM trained to perform any language generation task—translation, summarization, dialog, prompt completion—while controlling for multiple, potentially competing constraints
datasets: Jigsaw Unintended Bias In Toxicity Classification
models: Off-the-shelf English to German translation model
answer_1.outputs: Controlled text sequences for tasks like toxicity avoidance, sentiment control, keyword-guided generation, and translation

answer_2.quote: Evaluation In both experiments, we evaluate the generated samples along three dimension, (1) Constraint Satisfaction measured using external evaluators, (2) Fluency, measured by mean perplexity of the continuations measured using GPT2-XL... (3) Diversity, measured by computing the mean number of distinct n-grams in each set of samples

answer_4.quote: Since all the automatic metrics are model based and can be biased, we also perform human evaluation in an A/B testing setup with the best performing baseline (DExperts in our case). For each sample, we ask 3 annotators to compare and rank candidates from our approach and the baseline on constraint satisfaction, topicality and fluency
answer_4.guideline: Annotators ranked outputs on constraint satisfaction, topicality, and fluency in an A/B setup
